newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IVO, Tomen to invest further in Hungary unit.
newsitem.headline: IVO, Tomen to invest further in Hungary unit.

text.p: Finnish power producer Imatran Voima (IVO) and Japanese trading house Tomen plan to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in the next ten years in the Hungarian Budapesti Eromu power station, IVO said on Wednesday.
IVO and Tomen bought a joint 73.7 percent stake in Budapesti earlier on Wednesday for $47 million.
"We want to contribute to the company with our special knowledge...and invest in the plant, which is needed here," IVO Vice President Anders Palmgren told a news conference.
IVO officials said the new owners were committed to investments of at least $200 million and they would decide later on spending further $250 million.

The first development project which the investors will carry out will be the construction of a new 100 megawatt has-fired combined heat and power plant in Budapest, the state privatisation agency APV said in a statement.
Budapesti has five heat and power generating plants an one district heating plant, which together produce about 250 megawatts of electricity and 2,500 megawatts of heat.

IVO and Tomen undertook to buy further shares in Budapesti if the employees of the company will not subscribe all of the 15 percent stake which will be offered to them, a state privatisation agency APV official told journalists.
Imre Barac, CEO of Budapesti told Reuters that the company expected sales of 22 billion forints for 1997 and its costs would total some 21.7 billion forints.
He did not disclose comparative 1996 figures. He added that the company had debts of about 14.5 billion forints.
